metadata.notes: County and state segments are not separate tornadoes. All claims research-only; no final fact checks, approvals or visual licenses.

reviews.title_after: The Naplate–Ottawa EF3 tornado strikes northern Illinois
reviews.location_after: Utica–Naplate–Ottawa corridor, La Salle County, Illinois
reviews.core_fact: The February 28, 2017 Naplate–Ottawa tornado tracked from the Utica vicinity into Naplate and Ottawa; its strongest surveyed damage was EF3 near Naplate.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The NCEI Utica Airpark point is a location along this one tornado's path, not a separate EF3; the full track did not remain at EF3 intensity. Fatalities and exact track figures need survey reconciliation.
reviews.graphic_concept: Rebuild the tornado track with labeled EF0–EF3 damage segments and a February-climatology inset
reviews.graphic_data_source: NWS Chicago event track and SPC storm reports

reviews.title_after: A long-track EF4 tornado tears through the Yazoo City corridor
reviews.location_after: Tallulah, Louisiana to Yazoo City and central Mississippi
reviews.core_fact: An April 24, 2010 long-track tornado affected central Mississippi including the Yazoo City area, with EF4 damage documented in Yazoo and Holmes Counties.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The NCEI Enola entry is one county/location segment of the broader single track; do not assign EF4 to the entire track or sum county casualties. Early surveys were preliminary.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original single-track map with graded EF intensity segments and dated radar-debris-ball inset
reviews.graphic_data_source: NWS Jackson survey and archived radar imagery

reviews.title_after: The Parkersburg–New Hartford EF5 tornado devastates northeast Iowa
reviews.core_fact: On May 25, 2008, an EF5 tornado began south of Aplington and moved through Parkersburg and New Hartford, Iowa.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The source NCEI Aplington segment belongs to the same tornado; EF5 and a quoted 205-mph wind are damage-derived estimates, not a direct anemometer measurement. Do not mistake Butler County fatalities for extra tracks.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Aplington-to-Parkersburg intensity-gradient map from surveyed route data
reviews.graphic_data_source: NWS Des Moines tornado assessment and mapped track

reviews.title_after: An F4 tornado levels much of Spencer, South Dakota
reviews.location_after: Spencer and McCook County, South Dakota
reviews.core_fact: On May 30, 1998, a violent F4 tornado struck Spencer, South Dakota, after moving from nearby Hanson County.
reviews.unverified_cautions: This is a pre-2007 Fujita F4, NOT EF4. Some reports use CST for local records while federal assessment uses about 8:40 PM CDT; confirm time conventions and track continuity before graphics.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Spencer town damage-path diagram and accurate local-time chronology
reviews.graphic_data_source: NWS Sioux Falls official track and service assessment

reviews.title_after: An EF4 tornado carves through Freeborn County during Minnesota's historic outbreak
reviews.location_after: Mansfield–Conger–Albert Lea area, Freeborn County, Minnesota
reviews.core_fact: A tornado beginning near Mansfield, Minnesota, on June 17, 2010 intensified to EF4 in Freeborn County during a statewide tornado outbreak.
reviews.unverified_cautions: This is the Freeborn County/Conger tornado, not the separate Wadena EF4. The NCEI Mansfield segment should not be counted as an extra outbreak tornado. Statewide tornado totals depend on the review vintage.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Freeborn County track map contrasted against separate outbreak tracks
reviews.graphic_data_source: Minnesota DNR historical case summary and NWS Twin Cities radar

reviews.title_after: Charley's remnants unleash extreme rain and flooding around Del Rio
reviews.location_after: Del Rio and Val Verde County, southwest Texas
reviews.core_fact: On August 23, 1998, moisture from the remnants of Tropical Storm Charley generated devastating rainfall and flooding in the Del Rio, Texas area.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Tropical Storm Charley made its Texas landfall August 22, NOT August 23. USGS and Texas A&M report 17.03 inches at Del Rio on August 23, but station/clock and original observation must be inspected before using as a standalone quantified graphic.
reviews.graphic_concept: Del Rio original calendar-day rainfall bar plot versus pre-storm drought, with streamgage hydrograph if confirmed
reviews.graphic_data_source: USGS flood hydrology and Texas A&M climate bulletin

reviews.title_after: Hurricane Ian makes catastrophic southwest Florida landfall
reviews.location_after: Cayo Costa, Lee County and southwest Florida
reviews.core_fact: Hurricane Ian made landfall near Cayo Costa, southwest Florida, on September 28, 2022 as an extremely dangerous Category 4 hurricane.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The Cayo Costa island landfall and later mainland Florida landfall are separate timestamps on the same cyclone. Lee County Storm Data wind/gust and surveyed surge heights are not confirmed simply by the NHC position update; use updated tropical cyclone report for final values.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Ian track with island/mainland landfall timing and separately sourced peak surge measurements
reviews.graphic_data_source: NHC archived September 28 updates and latest TCR

reviews.title_after: A stalled boundary triggers the catastrophic October 1998 Texas floods
reviews.location_after: San Antonio and Guadalupe/San Antonio River basins, south-central Texas
reviews.core_fact: A major rainstorm October 17–18, 1998 caused severe floods in the Guadalupe and San Antonio river basins in south-central Texas.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The NCEI source may be one county flash-flood segment of a multi-day basin-wide event. Basin flood crests occurred across October 17–20; rainfall-day, storm total, stage, fatality and damage counts need explicit separate provenance.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original measured rain and USGS streamgage peak map; distinguish October 17 rain from downstream crest dates
reviews.graphic_data_source: USGS FS-147-99 gage tables and CDC storm-related mortality study

reviews.title_after: Santa Ana winds drive the start of the Witch Creek Fire
reviews.location_after: Witch Creek east of Ramona and San Diego County, California
reviews.core_fact: The Witch Creek Fire began east of Ramona on October 21, 2007 during a major Santa Ana wind event.
reviews.unverified_cautions: CAL FIRE's October 21 12:35 PM incident start and San Diego city fire retrospective date the incident; the eventual conflagration, fire mergers, evacuation and acres burned happened over days. Distinguish Witch from Guejito fire and confirm any ignition-causation claim independently.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original San Diego wind direction/gust and fire-growth map, explicitly separating 21st ignition from 22nd expansion
reviews.graphic_data_source: CAL FIRE incident details, municipal after-action report, station winds
reviews.title_before: Wildfire — SAN DIEGO COUNTY VALLEYS, California

reviews.title_after: Sandy's surge floods Staten Island as the post-tropical storm reaches the coast
reviews.location_after: Staten Island, New York Harbor and the New Jersey coast
reviews.core_fact: On October 29, 2012, Sandy caused destructive coastal inundation in and around Staten Island/New York Harbor while its center made landfall in New Jersey.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Sandy made landfall near the New Jersey shore as a post-tropical cyclone, NOT an active hurricane at landfall. New Jersey landfall site is not Staten Island. Report measured storm tide with datum; do not substitute surge for storm tide.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original high-water-mark map for Staten Island, annotated with New Jersey center track and tide-datum legend
reviews.graphic_data_source: USGS 2013-1043 station/sensor data and NHC landfall bulletin
reviews.title_before: Coastal Flood — RICHMOND (STATEN IS.), New York

reviews.title_after: The Saragossa F3 tornado crosses the Townley area of Alabama
reviews.location_after: Fayette, Walker and Winston Counties, Alabama
reviews.core_fact: On November 10, 2002, a long-track tornado identified by NWS Birmingham as the Saragossa tornado crossed the Townley area during the Veterans Day outbreak.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Townley is an NCEI location/segment within this tornado, not an extra F3. This storm was assigned a historical F3, not EF3. Separate this track from other tornadoes of the outbreak; county injury totals cannot be added indiscriminately.
reviews.graphic_concept: Reconstruct the Saragossa tornado track across county lines and timeline of outbreak warnings

reviews.title_after: An F3 tornado devastates Riegelwood, North Carolina
reviews.core_fact: On November 16, 2006, an F3 tornado hit Riegelwood in Columbus County, North Carolina, and continued along the county tornado track.
reviews.unverified_cautions: F3 is the original pre-2007 Fujita scale, NOT EF3. An F3 describes damage-inferred intensity; avoid unverified peak wind and county-vs-entire-track casualty totals. Confirm wake and time-zone issues before reconstructing radar.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Riegelwood track-over-community map with local radar/surface analysis
reviews.graphic_data_source: NWS Wilmington storm survey and historical climatology

reviews.title_after: Super Typhoon Pongsona's eye crosses Guam
reviews.core_fact: Super Typhoon Pongsona affected Guam on December 8, 2002, with its eye crossing the northern part of the island.
reviews.unverified_cautions: NASA's storm-wide 150-mph sustained/184-mph gust estimates differ from station-specific winds, which may have failed or used other periods. Do not label modeled storm maximum as an observed Guam station gust. TRMM satellite image date Dec7 is approach, not actual landfall Dec8.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Dec7-to-Dec8 satellite sequence with Guam locator and wind-observation caveats
reviews.graphic_data_source: NASA TRMM imagery and NOAA NWS Guam report

reviews.title_after: The Clarksville EF3 tornado tracks from Tennessee into Kentucky
reviews.core_fact: On December 9, 2023, an EF3 tornado began near Fort Campbell/Woodlawn, affected Clarksville, Tennessee and crossed into Kentucky.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The NCEI Woodlawn record is one section of the same cross-state tornado. Kentucky portions were generally assessed EF2 in NWS Paducah's jurisdiction; do not assume the entire long track was EF3 or transfer one state's casualties to the other.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original cross-state tornado track shaded by county rating and NWS office
reviews.graphic_data_source: NWS Nashville and Paducah surveyed track data

reviews.title_after: A New Year's Eve EF3 tornado hits Cincinnati, Arkansas
reviews.location_after: Westville, Oklahoma to Cincinnati and Benton County, Arkansas
reviews.core_fact: On December 31, 2010, a long-track EF3 tornado moved from eastern Oklahoma into Arkansas and hit Cincinnati in Washington County.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The Cincinnati NCEI record is the second of multiple county segments of the same tornado. NWS Norman reports four fatalities in Arkansas, not Oklahoma; avoid adding segment fatalities together or assigning all damage along the path EF3.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Westville-to-Cincinnati track timeline with state-line county transition
reviews.graphic_data_source: NWS Norman multi-state tornado track registry

claim_checks.evidence: NWS Chicago's dated tornado report and damage-intensity map
claim_checks.caution: EF3 was damage-rated near Naplate; not along the complete path
claim_checks.use: Use single surveyed track and precise EF damage locations

claim_checks.claim: Yazoo City violent tornado occurred on April 24 and reached EF4 in Yazoo/Holmes Counties
claim_checks.evidence: NWS Jackson survey shows continuous long track with regional EF4 spots
claim_checks.caution: NCEI Enola is a segment; do not sum segment impacts as separate tornadoes
claim_checks.use: Use regional single track and discrete EF4 points
